clue.text: Evocative of cars coming in late?

indicators.note: the cars are said to come into the other word, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: late in the sense of not long ago, recent
Minis are small British cars

explanation.surface: Someone muses on old cars rolling in at the last moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reminiscent calls up memories, which is what being evocative of a thing means.

clue.text: Laments English that is accepted by members

indicators.note: the letters are taken in by the limbs, going inside them

parts.note: legs are limbs, members of the body
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Laments in English are taken up by club members.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegies are mournful poems or songs of lament.

clue.text: Mingle where the fire may be after endless winter

indicators.note: after puts the fireplace word behind the trimmed season
endless means the season's word loses its end letters at both sides

parts.note: a grate holds the fire in a hearth

explanation.surface: People mix around the hearth after a long winter.
explanation.definitionFit: To integrate is to mix into a group, which is to mingle.

clue.text: A case of members supporting one million religious leaders

indicators.note: in a down clue the later letters sit beneath the first ones, holding them up

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the case is the outside, so only the first and last letters of the word are used

explanation.surface: A group of members back a million clerics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of members' gives MS, its outer letters; 'supporting' puts A MS below I M.
explanation.definitionFit: Imams lead prayers in a mosque and are leaders in Islam.

clue.text: Case yet to be developed for item pertaining to road safety

indicators.note: letters not yet developed are still to be worked into their final shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A road safety device is still at the planning stage.
explanation.walkthrough: CAT'S-EYES are reflective studs set into British roads to mark lanes at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's-eye is a reflector set in the road surface to guide drivers at night.

clue.text: Tolstoy losing heart after book's unexpected appearance

indicators.note: after puts the trimmed name behind the book

parts.note: a novel is a book; the 's here is is

indicators.note: losing its heart means all but the end letters of the name go

explanation.surface: A Tolstoy novel loses its emotional core, surprisingly.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelty is something new and unfamiliar, a fresh and surprising arrival.

clue.text: Prize awarded for a chef's aid?

definitions.text: Prize awarded for a chef's aid?

parts.words: Prize awarded for a chef's aid?
parts.note: the booby prize for coming last is named after a kitchen utensil used for stirring

explanation.definitionFit: The booby prize given to whoever finishes last is named after a cook's stirring utensil.

clue.text: A fine and equitable business

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
fair means just or equitable

explanation.surface: A fine and just matter is being handled.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair is a matter or concern, as in 'that's my business'.

clue.text: Unconventional females worn out by love

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
F is the abbreviation for female, doubled for the plural
beat is informal for exhausted

explanation.surface: Women exhausted by romance are an odd lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Offbeat is a synonym meaning unusual or departing from the norm.

clue.text: Live musical turns including Chopin's first

indicators.note: the reversed show takes another letter inside it
turns tells us the name of the musical is read backwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the composer's name is used

explanation.surface: A live show of musical numbers starts with Chopin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses EVITA to ATIVE, and 'including' puts C, the first letter of Chopin, inside it. 'musical turns' looks like song-and-dance acts.
explanation.definitionFit: Live and active are synonyms in the sense of being in operation or alive and working.

clue.text: Vets say something that might appear on monitor

definitions.text: something that might appear on monitor

parts.note: to vet is to check or screen
aver means to state or declare

explanation.surface: Vets claim to have seen something on a screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A screensaver is a moving image shown on an idle computer display.

clue.text: Trading area of London linked to Germany

indicators.note: linked to joins the borough to the country letter, which here comes first

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
Ealing is a district in west London

explanation.surface: A London borough is connected with a German business deal.
explanation.walkthrough: EALING is a suburb in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealing is a synonym of trading, as in buying and selling.

clue.text: The girl will shortly account for varnish

parts.note: the girl will contracts to she'll
shortly signals the abbreviation, and AC is short for account

explanation.surface: A girl promises to explain her varnishing job.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin used to make a kind of varnish.

clue.text: Scandinavian mostly adopting married standards

indicators.note: the shortened word takes another letter into itself
mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: Norse means Scandinavian, as in the old Norse peoples

explanation.surface: A Nordic nation takes on the customs of marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts NORSE to NORS, and 'adopting' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Norms are accepted standards of behaviour or practice, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: The original model of 'P' in layout of eye chart

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the rearranged letters
a layout is an arrangement, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: An optician's chart has the letter P placed on it as a template.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layout of' rearranges EYE CHART into ARCHETYE, and 'in' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is a first, typical example from which copies are made.

clue.text: Mostly relaxed, artist captures popular tree

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: casual means relaxed or informal

indicators.note: the artist's letters hold the other word inside

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A laid-back painter captures a well-loved tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'popular tree' reads as a favourite tree, but popular is the IN wordplay and tree alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A casuarina is an Australasian tree with drooping jointed twigs, also called she-oak.

clue.text: A blunt instrument might be useless

definitions.meaning: a blunt tool has lost its sharp tip, so it is literally without a point

explanation.definitionFit: Pointless means futile, and literally describes something whose sharp end is gone.

clue.text: Earnestly solicit the knowledge of the little people!

indicators.note: knowledge of the imps puts the sprite word before the lore word

parts.note: an imp is one of the fairy folk, the little people
lore is traditional knowledge

explanation.surface: Someone begs for the wisdom of fairies.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to beg someone urgently, a synonym of earnest soliciting.

clue.text: Tout's two notes on theory regularly ignored

parts.note: ti is a note of the sol-fa scale
PS is a postscript, a note added to a letter

indicators.note: every other letter is ignored, keeping alternate ones

explanation.surface: A racing tout relies on two notes and patchy theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly ignored' keeps TER from theory. Tout's means tout is.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipster sells racing tips, which is what a tout does.

clue.text: Hairdresser's lad crossing a line

indicators.note: the boy's word spans the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: a son is a boy or lad

explanation.surface: A boy at the barber's steps across a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon is a business premises for a hairdresser or beautician.

clue.text: Undermine rebellious brutes, grabbing victory

indicators.note: the rearranged letters seize the extra letter inside
rebellious letters will not stay in line, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unruly thugs seize a win to weaken the regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebellious' makes SUBERT from brutes, and 'grabbing' puts V inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To subvert is to weaken or overthrow, which is to undermine.

clue.text: Secure area on top of Ukrainian carriage

parts.note: to land something is to secure it, as a fish or deal

indicators.note: top of in a down clue picks the first letter

explanation.surface: Someone lands a deal for a Ukrainian carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding top.

clue.text: In theory working with soft food, exhibitor loses heart

parts.note: on means operating or working, as a switched-on machine is
pap is bland, soft food for babies

indicators.note: losing its heart means only the end letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: An exhibitor eating baby food gets downhearted.
explanation.definitionFit: On paper is an idiom meaning theoretically, rather than in practice.

clue.text: Lost colour on church spread

parts.note: dye that ran has bled and lost its colour

explanation.surface: A faded colour was spread over the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is a large farm or ranch in North American usage.

clue.text: Part of agenda in a blasted backward country

indicators.note: backward tells us the picked letters run in reverse order
part of says the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A section of a cursed agenda belongs to a backward nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' points to AINABLA inside 'agenda in a blasted', and 'backward' turns it round. 'backward country' looks like an insult but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Albania is a Balkan nation on the Adriatic.

clue.text: Man of God involved in blessing city

indicators.note: the saint is caught up inside the other word

parts.note: a boon is a blessing or benefit
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a holy man

explanation.surface: A clergyman takes part in blessing a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Boston is the capital of Massachusetts, and also a town in Lincolnshire.

clue.text: Repeat charge applied to unprotected sites

indicators.note: applied to sets the charge against the trimmed sites, which lead
something unprotected has lost its outer covering, so the word's end letters go

parts.note: a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: Fees keep being levied on insecure locations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' suggests an accusation or attack, but it is a price; 'unprotected' means the word has lost its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to do or say something again.

clue.text: Google Conservatives posse?

parts.note: to google is to look up, or search, online
the Conservatives are a political party

explanation.surface: Someone looks up the Tories online.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a group gathered to hunt for someone, just as rescuers sent looking for a missing person are.
